items.s: Slang means ____ words used by a particular group.
A song, a game or a video can ____ a word into a hundred countries.
Somebody hears a word, repeats it, and gives it a new ____.
Words like this make people feel ____.
Whether a word fits depends on the situation and the people, so it depends on the ____.

match.d: informal words used by a particular group
the people who watch, read or listen to something
the situation that helps explain a meaning
relaxed, and not suitable for official writing

items.s: Somebody ____ a photo in the group chat.
Ten minutes later you are ____ the word yourself.
Young people have always ____ this.
A dictionary cannot always ____ you where a word belongs.
Most new words will ____ gone by the summer.

tfn.s: Slang is only ever made up of completely new words.
tfn.why: The text says: "Others are ordinary words that have been given a different job"

tfn.s: A word can travel to many countries in a few days.
tfn.why: The text says: "can carry a word out of one town and into a hundred countries in a few days"

tfn.s: The group chat in the opening has seven people in it.
tfn.why: The text does not say how many people are in the chat

tfn.s: Slang can leave somebody outside a conversation.
tfn.why: The text says: "A word that includes your friends can leave somebody else standing outside the conversation"

tfn.s: The article says you must use every new word you hear.
tfn.why: The text says: "You do not have to use every new word you hear"

items.s: Slang can quietly tell everybody who is in and who is ____.
When an expression becomes huge on one platform, that is rarely where it ____.
The person who made a word famous is almost never the person who ____ it.
A phrase that is natural in a message can sound strange in a job ____.
Moving between those registers is a ____, not a sign that your English is fake.

match.d: the level of formality you use when speaking
saying the opposite of what you mean, often unkindly
recognition given to the person who did something
a word or phrase used in a particular way

items.s: The phrase ____ out of a rap song.
Dictionary.com ____ it the word of the year in October 2025.
A phrase from a game ____ up in a conversation at a bus stop.
Fluent speakers move between registers without ____ about it.
Asking what somebody ____ is the fastest way out of an awkward moment.

tfn.s: Dictionary.com chose the phrase as its 2025 word of the year.
tfn.why: The text says: "in October 2025 Dictionary.com made it the word of the year"

tfn.s: The platform where a word becomes popular is usually where it started.
tfn.why: The text says: "When an expression becomes huge on one platform, that platform is very rarely where it began"

tfn.s: The article names the school where the phrase was first used.
tfn.why: The text does not name a school

tfn.s: A word's meaning can shift as it travels.
tfn.why: The text says: "Along the way, the meaning often shifts. A word that started as a compliment can end up sarcastic"

tfn.s: The article says changing how you speak means one version of your English is fake.
tfn.why: The text says: "That switching is a skill, not evidence that one version of your English is fake"

items.s: Slang signals ____: you get the reference because you share a history.
The internet alters the ____ rather than the mechanism.
Visibility is not ____.
A great deal of English slang has been ____ for a general audience.
Admitting the ____ is more honest than crediting whoever went viral.

match.d: the fact of having created something
present something again in a new form
the style of language chosen to suit a situation
admit that something is true, often reluctantly

items.s: The same language that creates connection also draws a ____ around others.
A phrase can be repeated ____ or borrowed for a joke.
Sometimes the origin is genuinely hard to ____.
Learning to make that choice ____ is worth more than using the newest word.
Adults often hear unfamiliar slang as proof the language is ____.

tfn.s: Dictionary.com gave the phrase a clear and stable definition.
tfn.why: The text says: "while effectively conceding that it had no stable definition"

tfn.s: The article says the appeal of the phrase was the pleasure of being included.
tfn.why: The text says: "It was the pleasure of being in on something"

tfn.s: The article identifies the first person ever to say the phrase.
tfn.why: The text does not name anyone as the first speaker

tfn.s: Slang can create connection and exclude people at the same time.
tfn.why: The text says: "Both things happen at once, and usually nobody decides to do either"

tfn.s: The article argues young people should stop using informal English.
tfn.why: The text says: "being able to handle both widens your options instead of asking you to give one up"
